note: 2024 edition data, not updated. The series covers 2004–2024; intermediate points are approximate readings of the historical chart. FY25’s approximately 29% includes RLNG, imported coal, furnace oil and electricity imports. Its broader definition prevents a direct extension of this series.

title: Installed capacity versus seasonal demand
note: Updated to FY25 for installed capacity and served seasonal peaks. The dashed 23,000 MW average-demand line is 2024 edition data, not updated. Served peaks differ from NEPRA’s computed demand above 33,000 MW. Nameplate capacity is not continuously dispatchable spare power.

source: Renewables First / NEPRA; Energy Series (2024)

title: The annual cost of losses and unpaid bills
note: Updated to FY25 for the final bar: Rs. 265 billion in losses above allowed targets and Rs. 132 billion in under-recovery, excluding K-Electric. FY23–FY24 bars are 2024 edition data, not updated on a comparable basis. Later reports give different historical baselines and collection definitions, so the bars do not establish a comparable percentage decline. No FY26 performance series is supplied.
subtitle: Original stacked comparison extended to FY25.
source: NEPRA PER FY25; Energy Series (2024)

title: DISCO performance: physical and financial losses
note: Updated to FY25 using the supplied NEPRA performance-report figures. Financial losses measure breaches of allowed targets, not all lost electricity. The reported Rs. 265.01 billion total excludes K-Electric; the displayed companies do not reproduce the full aggregate. K-Electric’s Rs. 1.05 billion calculation is disputed. The 8% global reference is 2024 edition data, not updated.
subtitle: Loss rates and their financial impact, as two aligned panels.
source: NEPRA PER FY25
caption: Actual T&D loss rates and financial losses from exceeding allowed targets, FY25.

title: Pakistan’s network losses remain above the historical peer benchmarks
note: Updated to FY25 for Pakistan’s ex-WAPDA DISCO loss rate of 17.55%. Foreign rates and the 8% global reference are 2024 edition data, not updated; their underlying years and coverage are not harmonised. K-Electric’s separate FY25 rate is 14.73%.
subtitle: Pakistan: ex-WAPDA DISCOs, FY25. Other countries: original comparison, not updated.
source: Source: NEPRA PER FY25; historical peer figures from IPRI, Energy Series (2024).
caption: Pakistan: ex-WAPDA DISCOs, FY25. Other countries: original comparison, not updated.

title: Debt fell, then started accumulating again
note: Updated endpoints: Rs. 2,393 billion in June 2024, Rs. 1,614 billion in June 2025 and Rs. 1,675 billion in June 2026. Another official reply reports Rs. 1,641 billion for June 2025. Earlier points are 2024 edition data, not updated; intermediate values are approximate chart readings. The September 2025 refinancing occurred after the June 2025 reduction.
subtitle: Power-sector circular debt, PKR billion. Updated annual endpoints through June 2026.
source: Source: historical IPRI graphic; NEPRA / Power Division and October 2026 National Assembly reply.
caption: Power-sector circular debt, PKR billion. Updated annual endpoints through June 2026.

title: Electricity markets have moved towards more competitive structures
note: 2024 edition data, not updated. The historical comparison covers 1989 and 2024 and counts 230 jurisdictions in each year without defining coverage. Pakistan’s 2026 market opening is discussed separately.
subtitle: Number of jurisdictions, 1989 and 2024. Historical comparison, not updated.

caption: Number of jurisdictions, 1989 and 2024. Historical comparison, not updated.

title: The transport electrification opportunity
note: 2024 edition data, not updated. Vehicle counts and the 4,500 MW estimate describe an illustrative full-electrification scenario, not a forecast. Areas do not encode quantities. Actual demand and savings depend on adoption, charging patterns, efficiency and the generation mix.
subtitle: Original four-part transport illustration.
source: Energy Series (2024)
caption: Full-electrification scenario, 2024. These estimates are not an adoption forecast.

title: Industrial electricity sales recovered after the decline
note: Updated: all FY21–FY25 observations use Economic Survey 2025–26, Statistical Appendix Table 14.1, including revised FY21–FY23 values. FY23 sales fell 3.3% for households and 1.5% for industry. July–March FY26 figures in the text are partial-year observations and are not joined to this annual series.

source: Source: Pakistan Economic Survey 2025–26, Statistical Appendix Table 14.1.
caption: Full-year electricity sales, GWh. FY21–FY25 use Economic Survey 2025–26 totals.

note: Updated for the reported 2026 range of 10–12 US cents per watt. The 28-to-11-cent comparison is 2024 edition data, not updated; its precise endpoint dates are not specified. The shaded range is not a confidence interval. Panel prices exclude inverters, installation and batteries.
